answer: An agent economy deters Sybil attacks with slashable identity bonds. A shared registry called the atlas maps one bond to one agent identity; the protocol kernel slashes the full stake of any agent caught vouching for fake peers. To masquerade as a thousand workers, an attacker must fund a thousand bonds in quartz, so the cost grows linearly with each forged identity while honest agents split the same rewards. The fraud pays only when the attacker's staked quartz outweighs the honest stake.
